CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with severe pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a female presenting with severe left-sided back pain that began approximately three days ago. Pain is constant and has been radiating lower into the groin area. She denies passing the stone. Patient reports hematuria noted this morning. She has a history of recurrent kidney stones, this being her third episode. Previously, stones have passed within three to four days. Patient reports taking acetaminophen and ibuprofen with minimal relief. She also reports chills and nausea but denies fever. Patient states she is unable to eat due to pain severity.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Denies fever. Reports chills. Reports nausea. Reports hematuria. Able to urinate.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus
3. Recurrent kidney stones (third episode)
4. Systolic ejection murmur (Grade 2/6)

MEDICATIONS
1. Norvasc 2.5 mg daily for hypertension
2. Metformin 500 mg daily for diabetes
3. Acetaminophen as needed
4. Ibuprofen as needed

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys french fries and high-sodium foods. Obtained home blood pressure cuff but has not been consistently monitoring readings.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated, likely secondary to pain. Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted (known finding). Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes. Abdomen: Tender to palpation, no rebound or guarding. Costovertebral angle tenderness on the right flank bilaterally. Left-sided back pain on palpation.

RESULTS
Recent glucose test approximately two months ago: 300 mg/dL. Current fasting blood glucose readings: low 100s. Most recent A1C: 7.3. Blood pressure readings at home: systolic 130-150, diastolic 70-80. Current blood pressure in clinic: elevated.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Kidney stone, recurrent: Prescribe oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours as needed for pain. Continue acetaminophen for breakthrough pain. Encourage aggressive fluid intake to promote stone passage. Provide urine strainer to patient to collect stone if passed. Refer to urology for evaluation and prevention of future stones, even if stone passes within next few days.
2. Hypertension: Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. Blood pressure control adequate. Encouraged patient to reduce sodium intake to 2,300 mg per day and to continue home blood pressure monitoring at least three times per week.
3. Diabetes mellitus: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Home glucose monitoring showing good control in low 100s fasting range. Refer to dietitian/nutrition for dietary counseling and weight management to potentially reduce medication requirements in the future.
